title: AR-Order RL Post-Training Reduces Order Robustness in Diffusion Language Models

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to test whether autoregressive-order RL post-training compromises the order robustness that distinguishes diffusion LMs from AR models. Paper [3] explicitly investigates the order robustness of diffusion language models compared to autoregressive models, focusing on reasoning order and output order conflicts. This aligns substantively with the purpose of the contribution, as both aim to understand the impact of model architecture or training on order robustness.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves comparing robustness ratios across three models (diffusion base, AR-order RL trained, and AR anchor) using ReasonOrderQA and GSM8K benchmarks. Paper [16] conducts a systematic comparison of RL algorithms (including GRPO) for reasoning enhancement in LLMs, using controlled evaluations across reasoning benchmarks. While the specific benchmarks differ, the mechanism of comparing models using RL-trained variants and reasoning benchmarks is substantively equivalent.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design uses robustness ratios (r = Acc(AF)/Acc(CF)) on ReasonOrderQA and GSM8K, with a decision threshold of 0.10. Paper [24] introduces the Robust Reasoning Benchmark (RRB), which evaluates reasoning robustness across textual perturbations applied to mathematical benchmarks. Both designs assess robustness in reasoning tasks using deterministic metrics, making the evaluation design substantively equivalent.

### Domain
The domain is diffusion language models and RL post-training. Paper [14] introduces Dream 7B, a diffusion large language model, and discusses its performance on reasoning tasks, including arbitrary-order generation. Paper [4] surveys RL-based post-training methods for LLMs, including GRPO and PPO, which are relevant to the RL post-training aspect. Together, these papers cover the domain of diffusion LMs and RL post-training.
